draft.title: Cause and effect in economics
card: A cause is a change that makes something else happen. An effect is the change that follows.
A cause-and-effect relationship explains how one change leads to another. It links them in steps.
Example: a drought cuts the supply of fruit. With less fruit for sale, the price of fruit rises.
Two things can change at the same time without one causing the other. To claim a cause, you need a reason that explains the link.
draft.remember: A cause-and-effect link explains how one change leads to another.

a.q: A frost destroys much of a farm's strawberry crop, and the price of strawberries then rises. What is the cause?
opts: The frost destroying the strawberry crop
The price of strawberries rising
Shoppers noticing the higher price
Strawberries being sold in shops
a.why: The frost is the change that started the chain. Less fruit was available, so the price rose. The price rise is the effect, not the cause.
a.clue: Which change happened first and led to the others?

b.q: Ella notices that ice cream sales and sunburn cases both rise in summer. Which statement best explains a cause-and-effect link?
opts: Hot weather leads more people to buy ice cream
Ice cream sales cause more people to get sunburnt
Sunburn cases cause ice cream sales to rise
Both rose, so one must have caused the other
b.why: Hot weather gives a reason for people to buy ice cream, so it explains the link. Two things rising together does not show that one caused the other, which is why the last option is wrong.
b.clue: Look for the option that gives a reason for the link.

a.best: The frost destroying the strawberry crop

b.best: Hot weather leads more people to buy ice cream

problems.detail: The why says the 'last option' is wrong because two things rising together does not show causation. That reasoning fits 'Both rose, so one must have caused the other', not the option shown last ('Sunburn cases cause ice cream sales to rise'). Options are shuffled, so the why should name the option, not its position.

The stem asks which statement 'best explains a cause-and-effect link' without saying which link. The right option brings in hot weather, which the stem never mentions, and it explains only ice cream sales, not sunburn. The card does not teach that a third factor can cause both changes, so some students may be confused about what is being asked.
